competences: The learner identifies key facts about members of the district council.
The learner explains the roles of district leaders using the sourced local-government materials.
languageCompetence: Learners read, write and pronounce: leader, councillor, district, local government, speaker, civic and political.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to name the members of district councils and describe their roles.
By the end of the lesson learners should be able to answer original source questions about district leadership.
priorKnowledge: Learners understand political and civic leaders, councils and their responsibilities.
materials: P4 SST school reference notes on district leadership
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the preceding lesson on district leadership and asks "Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee.". They use the pupils' answers to connect earlier material to members of the district council.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous Social Studies period, answer the opening question and identify leaders within their local council.

steps.stage: Development: Members of a district council
steps.content: The district council has a chairperson. The district council has a vice chairperson. There are councillors for the youths. There are councillors for people with disabilities. Councillors represent sub-counties, divisions and towns. The district council has a secretary. The district council has a speaker. The district council has a deputy speaker.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Members of a district council", including "The district council has a chairperson. The district council has a vice chairperson." They explain the roles and ask "State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties." to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.stage: Development: Work of the district council
steps.content: The district council plans development projects. It governs local councils in the district. The district chairperson coordinates council activities. The district chairperson supervises district officials. The chairperson monitors district administration.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Work of the district council", including "The district council plans development projects. It governs local councils in the district." They explain the roles and ask "State any one role played by the district speaker." to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: The speaker presides over district council meetings. The district chairperson supervises local officials. The district secretary assists administration. Councillors represent people from their areas. The district council supports local government work. The RDC coordinates central-government programmes.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Duties of district officials", including "The speaker presides over district council meetings. The district chairperson supervises local officials." They explain the roles and ask "Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village." to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee. | State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties. | State any one role played by the district speaker. | Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original sourced questions, beginning with "Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee." and "State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties.". They supervise learners' written responses and check their answers against the leadership notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise independently, consult the facts in their notes and correct inaccurate answers after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher evaluates learning using "State any one role played by the district speaker." and "Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village.". They recap the source-grounded points and assign the remaining revision question for later practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one important district-leadership duty and correct their work in their books.

assessment: Check written and oral responses to "Apart from the chairperson, mention any three other members on the LC I executive committee.", "State any three problems district leaders face when carrying out their duties.", and "State any one role played by the district speaker." and mark against the source material.
homework: Complete the sourced question "Mention any three roles played by the LC I council in the village." in the Social Studies book.
